name: Markaz (Kuwait Financial Centre)
ownership_summary: Listed on the Boursa Kuwait Main Market (security code 213). The company's Q1 2026 investor presentation (18 May 2026) names two major shareholders: Kuwait Pillars for Financial Investment (27.72%, direct) and Al Mubader Co (5.13%, direct). Issued share capital is KWD 50.48m; shares outstanding were 466,658,228 per the May 2026 deck. Seven board members (3 independent per the May 2026 deck).
government_link: No government shareholding disclosed in company materials (checked 2026-10-12). Commercial link only: Markaz manages part of the Kuwait Investment Authority's National Real Estate Portfolio (described as the Real Estate Income Generating Portfolio, value up to KD 200m, in the Q1 2026 deck).
group_structure: Kuwait Financial Centre K.P.S.C. is the listed parent and runs asset management, wealth management, investment banking and real estate itself. Subsidiaries named in the 2026 profile: Mar-Gulf Management, Inc. (Los Angeles; coordinates US real estate since 1998) and Marmore MENA Intelligence (India; majority-owned research and consulting arm, est. 2010). Consolidated accounts include non-controlling interests (KD 7.9m at 31 Dec 2025). Markaz-managed funds include MIDAF, Mumtaz, Forsa Financial Fund, Markaz Arabian Fund, Markaz Islamic Fund, GCC Momentum Fund, Markaz Fixed Income Fund and Markaz Real Estate Fund (MREF). Board (2026 profile): Diraar Y. Alghanim (Chairman), Faisal AbdulAziz Al-Jallal (Vice Chairman), Adel M. Alghannam, Omran Habib Hayat, Ayman Abdulatif Alshaya, Mohammed Saad AlSaad, Fahad Yaqoub Al-Jouan.

subsidiaries.activity: US real estate investment coordination and management (Los Angeles)

footprint: Headquartered in Kuwait. 150+ employees with offices across the Middle East, the US and India (Q1 2026 deck). Company states a presence in 13 countries and investments in 15+ countries (2026 profile). Equity, fixed income, advisory and real estate activity across the GCC, Egypt, Lebanon, Germany, Poland, UK, India and USA.
customer_segments: Institutional (government and private), corporates, family offices and high-net-worth clients (H1 2026 release: focus on 'institutional and high net worth client relationships'), plus retail investors through mutual funds and the iMarkaz Invest self-directed trading platform.
business_lines: Asset management (GCC equity funds and discretionary portfolios, GCC fixed income fund and programmes, Islamic fund); real estate investment (MENA income-generating real estate incl. MREF and the KIA mandate; US/Europe development and industrial programmes); wealth management and business development (incl. Global Investment Advisory: bespoke investment policy and third-party manager selection); investment banking (ECM/DCM, M&A, restructuring, valuations); market making, margin lending and securities lending & borrowing; custody; digital trading via iMarkaz Invest (Kuwait, KSA, UAE, US); research via Marmore.

capabilities.wealth_summary: Markaz is a Kuwaiti listed asset manager and investment bank with KD 1.57bn of AUM at 30 Jun 2026. AUM is concentrated in GCC equities (KD 840m at Mar 2026), GCC fixed income (KD 125m) and MENA/international real estate (KD 402m). The product shelf is mostly its own funds and discretionary portfolios: MIDAF, Mumtaz, Forsa (options market maker), Markaz Arabian, Markaz Islamic Fund, GCC Momentum Fund, Markaz Fixed Income Fund and MREF, plus Opportunistic, Dividend and Plain Vanilla portfolios. A Global Investment Advisory team builds bespoke investment policies and selects third-party managers after due diligence. Private credit (2024) and a Private Real Assets strategy for qualified investors (2025) were launched. In March 2026 it launched iMarkaz Invest for self-directed trading in Kuwait, KSA, UAE and US markets, adding 24-hour US access in mid-2026. In Jan 2025 it selected Objectway's client-facing wealth solution.

segments.name: Wealth Management (institutional, family office and HNW relationships)

private_banking.detail: Not a bank. Wealth Management department (head: Deena Al-Refai, from May 2026) serves HNW, family office and institutional clients with discretionary portfolios, advisory and access to private and international products. Company materials cite 'Best Private Bank in Kuwait' (Global Finance) and 'Best Domestic Private Bank' (2023) awards.

asset_management.detail: Core business. AUM KD 1.57bn (30 Jun 2026). Own funds: MIDAF, Mumtaz, Forsa Financial Fund, Markaz Arabian Fund, Markaz Islamic Fund, GCC Momentum Fund (2023), Markaz Fixed Income Fund, MREF (KD 79m, 16 properties). Discretionary portfolios. Manages part of KIA's National Real Estate Portfolio. FY2025 asset-management fees KD 9.33m.

brokerage.detail: iMarkaz Invest (launched 28 Mar 2026): self-directed trading in Kuwait, Saudi, UAE and US markets via web portal and mobile app, with optional advisory from Wealth Management. 24-hour trading in eligible US equities/ETFs added mid-2026. Also market maker and margin lending services (2020–21) and securities lending & borrowing (2023). Executing broker/technology vendor and the exact CMA licence category were not found.

digital_investing.detail: iMarkaz app (launched 2020–21; digital onboarding) and iMarkaz Invest trading platform (Mar 2026) with real-time dashboards, digital account opening and real-time market data. Company cites Euromoney 'Best for Digital Solutions in Kuwait' (2024).

advisory.detail: Wealth management advisory and a Global Investment Advisory unit (EVP Kashish Tandon) providing bespoke investment policy planning, asset allocation and third-party manager selection. Investment banking advisory (M&A, restructuring, valuations) for corporates and family offices.

discretionary.detail: Managed private portfolios: Opportunistic, Dividend-yield and Plain Vanilla equity portfolios; risk-driven fixed income portfolios. AUM includes 'Private Portfolios'.

model_portfolios_robo.detail: No robo-advisor or digital model-portfolio service found. iMarkaz Invest is self-directed trading. The historical Atlas ETFs Portfolio (2000s) is not evidenced as current.

funds_platform.detail: International advisory gives access to 'leading 3rd party asset managers' selected through due diligence, with 'strategic relationships with leading international asset managers and GPs'. Historical example: Markaz Hamilton Lane Technology Fund of Funds (2000–05). No named fund-platform provider.

structured_products.detail: No structured notes found in the profile, decks or 2026 releases. Investment banking has arranged convertible bonds (2023) and the Forsa Financial Fund is an options market maker, but these are not client structured products.

private_markets.detail: Private Credit (launched 2024); Private Real Assets strategy for qualified investors (2025); US/Europe real estate development programmes (e.g. USD 7m commitment to a Phoenix industrial project, Q1 2026); International Private Equity Funds programme (historical). H1 2026 release says it is pursuing private credit, private infrastructure and development financing and broadening private markets, alternatives and advisory.

islamic_wealth.detail: Markaz Islamic Fund (MIF). FY2025 CEO statement refers to 'specialist Sharia-compliant products'. Markaz is a conventional firm with no Islamic window.

discrepancies.resolution: People list keeps the Chairman and Vice Chairman (both unchanged). Unresolved; AlSaad's appointment date and Aldalali's departure are not recorded.

open_items: markaz.com HTML pages (news, IR, leadership) sit behind a Cloudflare bot-check, which was not bypassed. PDFs under /getmedia/ were readable. The H1 2026 deck and interim statements URLs were not found in search; get them to verify 30 Jun 2026 total assets/equity.
Boursa Kuwait disclosure documents (docs.boursakuwait.com.kw) and Kamco research PDFs returned 403.

CMA Kuwait licensed-companies register was unavailable ('temporarily unavailable'), so Markaz's exact licensed activities (incl. broker/custodian categories behind iMarkaz Invest and custody) are unverified. The company states it is regulated by CMA and CBK (S1 disclaimer).
iMarkaz Invest execution broker and technology vendor not disclosed. The Objectway go-live status (announced Jan 2025) is not confirmed.
Aggregator pages (not cited) list Markaz Fund for Excellent Yields (Mumtaz) with about 13% of Markaz shares. Check the Boursa Kuwait major-shareholder disclosures.
Q3 2026 (30 Sep 2026) results not yet published as of 12 Oct 2026.

People pass X05 (2026-10-12): markaz.com HTML (leadership bios, subsidiaries, news, material information), docs.boursakuwait.com.kw and Albawaba answer 403; Alanba PDFs are image-only. Education/career for the executives (Al-Nusif, Al-Refai, Tandon, Al-Osaimi, Salamoun, Olayan, Al Rifae, Abrar, Al-Falah, Elia, Raghu, Shabshab) could not be filled: AR 2025 has board bios only; profiles give names and titles only. Re-run when https://www.markaz.com/en/who-we-are/leadership/ is reachable.

8 Apr 2026 AGM: the 12 Apr 2026 disclosure (results and minutes) was not found as a /getmedia/ PDF, so the apparent board election (Mohammed Saad AlSaad in, Fahad Sulaiman Aldalali out) and any re-election dates for the Chairman and Vice Chairman are unverified. Check Boursa Kuwait disclosures for security 213.
